summary: Current 40-foot R-6 timber lookout on Porphyry Peak, Lewis and Clark National Forest, staffed every summer; sources disagree on whether the first tower dates from 1933 or 1937.

facts.design: 40-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab

events.note: Two 1933 newspaper items, quoted on Forest Lookouts, describe a 40-foot tower built on Porphyry Peak; the Register and firelookout.com date first development to 1937
Lookout on Porphyry Mountain first noticed a fire in the Moose Creek area, a blind spot for the Helena lookouts
First developed with a 40-foot pole L-4 tower, per the Register and firelookout.com
Porphyry and Williams Mountain lookouts reported a fire near Black Butte; a county crew was sent to fight it
Don and Adair Peterson, married the previous June, were Forest Service fire lookouts here; no fires spotted yet at the time of the article
The present 40-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab replaced the earlier tower
Registered April 12, 2022; nominated by Kyle Stetler

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1960 is the current tower, which the Register and the Forest Lookouts page both give. The 1933 newspaper items and the 1937 date from the Register and firelookout.com disagree about the first tower, and the 1937 article describes 50-foot towers where the other sources give 40 feet. The sources are not reconciled.

The Register says Cascade County and firelookout.com says Cascade/Meagher; the National Geodetic Survey station description places the station on the boundary between the two. The record keeps Cascade.
firelookout.com says about six miles south of Neihart; an August 1968 item quoted on Forest Lookouts says eight miles. The sources are not reconciled; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: The build history is disputed. The 1933 items and the 1937 article are quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; I did not check them against the original newspapers. The Register and firelookout.com give 1937 for first development. The 1937 article's 50-foot plan conflicts with the 40-foot height. The staffing note 'every summer' is undated in both the Register and firelookout.com, so no as_of was given. The record's access 'unknown' is kept; no source gives access or climbing status. The record's 1960 build year is the current tower and is supported by NHLR, so I proposed no correction. No new photos. Two web searches were not needed for this tower.
